items.body: Euclidean Spin(4) is decomposed into two chiral SU(2) factors in the Euclidean-first proposal.
Twistor space is C^4 / projective CP^3 with an SU(2,2) real form giving positive, negative, and null/boundary orbits for the Minkowski picture.
W04e proposes a new conjugation-like structure interchanging positive/negative imaginary-time sectors while preserving a Lorentzian-chiral subspace.

W01 fixes the Euclidean vector real form inside M(2,C) by the Pauli-matrix map, with determinant equal to positive Euclidean norm squared and an equivalent quaternion presentation with the quaternion norm x conjugate(x), with x a quaternion here rather than the distinct matrix carrier. W01 §2.1 prints the exact Euclidean matrix model x=x0*1-i(x1*sigma1+x2*sigma2+x3*sigma3), |x|^2=det(x), and the quaternion coordinate model x=x0*1+x1*i+x2*j+x3*k with |x|^2=x*conjugate(x). The preceding token KAPPA(x) is NOT the source-printed quaternion conjugate and is superseded here, not treated as a new operation.

W01 represents Spin(4) by independent left/right SU(2)=Sp(1) actions, with the Euclidean vector action x -> g_L x g_R^{-1}; the two factors are structurally independent in Euclidean signature. W01 §2.1 explicitly prints x maps to g_L*x*g_R^(-1) for Euclidean SU(2) left/right factors and says (g_L,g_R) and (-g_L,-g_R) determine the same SO(4) rotation, giving the source Spin(4) double-cover claim. The sign-paired representatives are not identical Spin-group elements. In the quaternion presentation SU(2)=Sp(1) is the unit-quaternion group with independent left and right multiplication and the imaginary-time coordinate maps to the identity.

All three real spaces complexify to M(2,C), but they do not carry the same real-form constraint. The printed Minkowski Lorentz action is x maps to inverse(adjoint(g)) * x * inverse(g) for g in SL(2,C); the split-signature Spin(2,2)=SL(2,R)_L x SL(2,R)_R action is x maps to g_L*x*inverse(g_R). These typed group actions differ from the Euclidean Spin(4) real-form action, even though complexification is shared. W01 §2.2 separately states spinor carriers S_R,S_L with complexified vectors Hom(S_R,S_L), using R2 in split E(2,2) but C2 for E4 and E3,1. In Euclidean E4 the two spinor spaces transform independently, whereas Minkowski SL(2,C) action g on S_R forces the (g^dagger)^(-1) action on S_L. A twistor spacetime point is a C2 plane S_R inside T=C4, with its point-relative quotient S_L=T/S_R and tangent Hom(S_R,S_L). The complex Grassmannian G_2,4(C) carries the SL(4,C) conformal action with source-ordered real subgroup/compactification correspondences Spin(5,1)/E4/S4, Spin(4,2)/E3,1/(S3×S1), Spin(3,3)/E2,2/G_2,4(R); do not equate the real forms or promote source claims to new proofs.

items.body: Appendix A defines alpha-planes from a twistor point and states that two spacetime points incident with the same projective twistor have null separation in the determinant quadratic form. Appendix A distinguishes the Penrose transform for massless helicity equations from the Penrose-Ward extension with gauge fields, including open-set and fiber-triviality side conditions. Appendix A distinguishes split, Minkowski, Euclidean, and compact SU(4) real-form structures of SL(4,C), each with different fixed/orbit/signature conditions; these real forms may not be collapsed into one representation.

For Minkowski twistor geometry W01 uses a signature-(2,2) Hermitian form Phi, anti-Hermitian affine coordinates, the SU(2,2) orbit decomposition of M/PT, and conjugate-dual left/right spinor actions. The source's App. A.3.2 states that SU(2,2) has 'six orbits' on M, then visibly lists ONLY FIVE named entries M_(++), M_(--), M_(+0), M_(-0), M_(00). Preserve the author's printed count FIVE-LISTED versus SIX-CLAIMED as an unresolved source inconsistency, without adding an imagined sixth orbit. The projective twistor PT partition is separately the three named orbits PT_+, PT_-, PT_0 with PT_0 a closed five-real-dimensional orbit; do not conflate the two orbit carriers.

For Euclidean twistor geometry W01 uses T=H^2, the pseudoreal map sigma with sigma^2=-1 on T and +1 projectively, HP1 homogeneous coordinates, SL(2,H) fractional-linear action, and the CP1 fibration whose sigma action is antipodal on each fiber. Appendix A.3.3 prints the source pseudoreal map sigma on four complex twistor coordinates as ordered (-bar(s2),bar(s1),-bar(s2^perp),bar(s1^perp)); sigma squared is -identity on T=C4 but +identity projectively on PT, with NO fixed twistor points; the induced quaternionic-line map fixes HP1 base points and acts antipodally on CP1 fibers. This map is a distinct typed instance from W05's rho_tw even when their fiber behaviors correspond.

Appendix B treats reconstruction of physical states from Euclidean data as requiring a chosen imaginary-time half-space/reflection and states that the resulting distinction between positive and negative imaginary time breaks SO(4) despite SO(4)-invariant Schwinger functions. Appendix B's source-specific Osterwalder-Schrader convention chooses the imaginary-time coordinate tau and the subspace E1^+ consisting of functions supported at tau<0, defines time reflection Theta f(tau,x)=f(-tau,x), then H1 as the quotient by the OS-null space; a different source's positive-time convention must not be silently substituted. In B.2 the free scalar Schwinger function is separately displayed in position space as m/((2*pi)^3*sqrt(tau^2+|x|^2))*K1(m*sqrt(tau^2+|x|^2)); analytic continuation has two t-axis branch cuts beginning at +/-|x|. items.body: W04a writes a right-handed Minkowski Weyl equation of the form (E-sigma dot p) psi_R=0, derives the Klein-Gordon mass-shell consequence, and associates its positive- and negative-energy branches with opposite helicities. It prints the energy-momentum equation (E-sigma·p) tilde_psi_R(E,p)=0, the ordered factorization (E+sigma·p)(E-sigma·p)=E^2-|p|^2, the conditional mass shell E=±|p|, and the helicity operator (1/2)(sigma·p)/|p| with +1/2 for positive-energy particles and -1/2 for negative-energy antiparticles; these are source-written roles, not qualified lower physical laws.

W04a contrasts the right-handed Minkowski Wightman kernel with the naive Euclidean substitution and makes the failure of a one-chirality Euclidean propagator/Lagrangian a concrete Wick-rotation obstruction. The displayed source Wightman formula is tilde_W2(E,p)=(E-sigma·p)^(-1)=(E+sigma·p)/(E^2-|p|^2), while the candidate naive Schwinger continuation is tilde_S2(E,p)=(iE-sigma·p)^(-1). The second is expressly an unsuccessful conventional Wick-rotation attempt, not an established continuation; the source's conventional vector operator is a map from S_R^* to S_L and the proposed right-handed-only replacement is separate.

In the conventional four-dimensional spinor-vector description W04a represents a complex vector as a map from the dual right spinor to the left spinor; Minkowski reality relates the two chiralities by conjugation whereas Euclidean signature leaves them independent.

In the CP1 analogue W04b uses the three SU(1,1)=SL(2,R) orbits and hyperfunction boundary values to model the relation between holomorphic domains and Lorentzian boundary data. The three CP1 split-real-form orbits are CP1+ upper hemisphere, CP1- lower hemisphere, and the S1 equator. W04b describes infinite-dimensional unitary discrete-series representations on holomorphic line-bundle sections over either open orbit or H1 cohomology. Boundary function spaces admit different choices, with hyperfunctions described as natural rather than uniquely forced. The Cayley transform relates SL(2,R) upper/lower-half-plane and real-axis actions to SU(1,1) CP1 actions; SL(2,Z) is a number-theory subgroup context, not additional twistor structure. Preserve printed SL(2,R)=SU(1,1) without mathematical normalization.

items.body: W04d identifies the spectral positivity of time evolution with holomorphy of U(z)=exp(-izH) in a complex-time half-plane and treats this holomorphic-domain structure as the operational core of Wick rotation. W04d explicitly writes U(t)=e^(-itH), z=t+is and U(z)=e^(-izH), and attributes holomorphy to energy positivity in the LOWER complex-time half-plane (s<0); the negative-imaginary-time axis is only one possible restriction, not a unique Wick-rotation target.

W04e instead uses an antilinear reflection/conjugation Theta associated with imaginary-time reflection in Osterwalder-Schrader reconstruction; the Hilbert-space inner product and physical state space are reconstructed from this reflection-positive Euclidean structure. Source §3 defines (\Theta f(\tau)=\overline{f(-\tau)}) as an antilinear involution (\Theta^2=1), on imaginary-time functions, and the free-field OS form by (\langle f,g\rangle_{OS}=S_2(\Theta f,g)), with positive-time support; no generic four-dimensional twistor-theory Theta is constructed here.

The W04e reconstruction requires choosing an imaginary-time half-space/direction and reflection, so the physical-state reconstruction breaks Euclidean SO(4) even when the underlying Euclidean correlation data are SO(4)-covariant.

In the twistor version W04e uses a Hermitian form Phi to split projective twistor space into positive, negative, and null regions; holomorphic theory on PT+ is proposed to have boundary values on the null region representing chiral Minkowski data, with Penrose/Penrose-Ward constructions supplying part of the reconstruction machinery. In these July notes the null orbit is specifically named (PN), alongside (PT^{+}) and (PT^{-}): the sign of (\Phi) partitions the projective (PT=CP^3), and the chosen (PT^{+}\to PN) boundary-value construction remains proposed, not qualified dynamical completeness.

W04d explicitly contrasts the conventional complex vector carrier S_L tensor S_R with the proposed right-handed carrier S_R tensor conjugate(S_R); on the Euclidean slice the latter decomposes as a scalar plus a three-vector and SU(2)_L acts trivially. Slide 17 explicitly presents the proposed complex carrier (S_R\otimes\overline{S_R}) but separately *prints* the Euclidean decomposition as (S_R\otimes S_R=1\oplus V_3) with no bar in the latter displayed line. The two printed expressions must remain distinct rather than silently adding a conjugation bar to the second, while SU(2)_L acts trivially only in that proposed role assignment.

W04d identifies conformally compactified complex spacetime with Gr(2,4,C), a spacetime point with a right-handed C2 plane in T=C4, and projective twistor space with CP3 containing the corresponding CP1.

W04d lists SU(4), SL(4,R), SL(2,H), and SU(2,2) as real forms of SL(4,C)=Spin(6,C), with the SL(2,H) and SU(2,2) forms assigned Euclidean and Minkowski geometric roles respectively. This is scoped to the signature-(2,2) Hermitian-null twistor real form, not all projective twistor structures.

Under the Euclidean SL(2,H) real form W04d uses T=C4=H2 and the CP3->HP1=S4 fibration sending each complex line to the quaternionic line it generates. Slide 25 prints the conditional quaternionic fibration (CP^1\to PT=CP^3\xrightarrow{\pi}S^4=HP^1), where (\pi) sends each complex line in (\mathbb C^4) to the quaternionic line it generates after *choosing* (T=\mathbb C^4=\mathbb H^2); the source does not assert that this chosen fibration is canonically fixed.

W04d gives two equivalent geometric roles for Euclidean PT: the projective right-spin bundle and the bundle of orthogonal complex structures on S4; it states that the latter construction extends to four-dimensional Riemannian manifolds and becomes a complex twistor space for anti-self-dual metrics.

W05 defines a real structure on CP1 as an antiholomorphic map rho: CP1 -> CP1 with rho squared equal to 1. The ordinary real structure is complex conjugation rho([z1,z2])=[bar(z1),bar(z2)]; its real points are exactly the points fixed by rho, forming a circle in CP1 (the real line in the affine z coordinate). W05 explicitly contrasts this ordinary real structure with the twistor antipodal real structure rho_tw, defined by rho_tw([z1,z2])=[-bar(z2),bar(z1)] (equivalently rho_tw(z)=-1/bar(z)); on C2 coordinates rho_tw squared equals -1, while on projective points rho_tw squared equals 1, and on the sphere rho_tw is the antipodal map with no projective fixed points. W05 also presents the same twistor P1 as the real projective conic x^2+y^2+z^2=0 in projective two-space, defined over the real numbers, with complex points but no real points. W05 explicitly identifies the Riemann sphere CP1 with complex lines in C2: homogeneous [z1,z2] denotes an equivalence class of pairs of complex numbers, and the affine coordinate chart z=z1/z2 identifies C with CP1 minus the point [z1,0]. For ordinary conjugation W05 also gives rho(z)=bar(z) in this affine chart. For the twistor map, W05 explicitly shows that the fixed-point equation z=-1/bar(z) would imply |z|^2=-1, a contradiction for a complex number. W05 furthermore describes the twistor P1 as the complex projective variety CP1 equipped with an action of Gal(C/R) and separately as the equation-defined real projective conic; these are its two source-given presentations. W05 writes the ordinary homogeneous real-point fixed-point equation rho([z1,z2])=[z1,z2] as the criterion for a real point of the ordinary structure. W05 also explicitly states that no projective point satisfies the homogeneous twistor fixed-point equation rho_tw([z1,z2])=[z1,z2]; this equation occurs under the source's negated existence claim, not as an asserted positive fixed point. In this W05 §2 source statement, rho_tw is itself the declared antiholomorphic CP1 real-structure MAP with source-given homogeneous arguments and outputs, not an optional relation restricted to witnessed two-step applications. Its map-type CP1 domain/codomain, projective-square identity, and projective fixed-point nonexistence are separate source obligations; the coordinate-level square-minus-identity and affine formula are distinct carrier/chart clauses and do not replace the projective type law.
